headline: Saudi attacks on boats in Yemen's Taiz kills eight fishermen
body:
What happened: Saudi strikes hit boats off al-Kadha in Yemen's Taiz Governorate, killing eight fishermen, according to Yemen's Ministry of Health and Environment. The ministry called the attack a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law. The incident adds to tensions over Saudi military action inside Yemen.

Reported by: Middle East Eye

actors.why: Eight civilian fishermen killed; government calls strikes illegal
Accused of striking civilians, facing international legal criticism

points: Saudi strikes hit boats near al-Kadha, in Yemen.
Eight fishermen were killed in the attacks.
Yemen's health ministry says the strikes broke international law.
impactPoints: Fishing families in Taiz lose their breadwinners and livelihoods.
Yemen's government and its allies accuse Saudi Arabia of harming civilians.
Saudi Arabia faces more criticism over its military campaign in Yemen.

headline: Ordinary day, extraordinary times: Kyiv under Russian attack
body:
What happened: Russia is stepping up drone attacks on Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, killing more than 190 people there since January. The article follows a Kyiv mother whose days are shaped by air raid alerts and explosions. The reporting shows the ongoing strain of the war on civilians in the capital.

Reported by: Japan Times. Also covered by Kyiv Independent.

actors.why: Capital Kyiv hit by drones, killing many civilians and disrupting life.
Stepped-up drone attacks on Kyiv, drawing criticism but advancing its campaign.

points: Russia has increased drone attacks on Kyiv since late summer.
Over 190 people have died in Kyiv from attacks since January.
Air raid alerts now disrupt daily life for ordinary families.
impactPoints: Kyiv residents face constant danger, stress and disrupted daily routines.
Ukraine's capital faces heavier losses and strain on services.
Russia's campaign keeps the war's human cost high for both sides.

headline: Iran war live: US warns peace deal with Tehran is extremely difficult
body:
What happened: The United States has warned that reaching a peace deal with Iran will be extremely difficult. The warning comes amid an ongoing conflict involving Tehran, and it matters because a deal could shape the security of the wider Middle East.

Reported by: Al Jazeera

actors.why: Iran is a direct party whose peace talks are described as very hard.
The US is a direct party warning that a peace deal is extremely difficult.

points: The US says a peace agreement with Iran is very hard.
The conflict involving Iran is still ongoing.
Talks face serious obstacles, according to Washington.
impactPoints: Iran faces pressure to make concessions to end the conflict.
The US faces difficulty achieving its goal of ending the fighting.
Neighbouring Gulf states could be drawn into or affected by the conflict.

headline: Musk ordered slowdown of Starlink service Ukraine military relies on, report says
body:
What happened: Elon Musk reportedly ordered a slowdown of a military-grade Starlink service that Ukraine uses for battlefield communications and drones. The move reportedly hampered Ukraine's drone attacks on Russia and air defence. Musk and Trump reportedly discussed the decision, and the report says US officials were involved.

Reported by: SCMP. Also covered by The Hindu.

actors.why: Military communications and drone operations were reportedly hampered by the slowdown.
Ukraine's drone attacks on Russia were reportedly weakened, easing pressure on Moscow.
Trump and US military reportedly shaped the decision, drawing scrutiny over control of the system.

points: Musk reportedly ordered a slowdown of Starlink's military internet service.
Ukraine uses this service to talk on the battlefield.
Ukraine also uses it to fly drones, including for attacks on Russia.
impactPoints: Ukraine's drone missions against Russia were reportedly held back.
Ukraine's battlefield communications could be weaker without the service.
Russia could benefit if Ukraine's drone attacks slow down.
US officials and Trump are linked to the decision, raising questions about US control.

headline: ‘I don’t care how it’s done’: Trump pressures Ukraine to cut peace deal
body:
What happened: US President Donald Trump is pressing Ukraine to agree a deal to end the war with Russia, blaming President Zelenskyy for delays. Talks in Oslo with European leaders and US envoy Steve Witkoff continue, with Witkoff heading to Moscow next.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Kyiv Independent, SCMP.

actors.why: Pressured to accept a deal while losing satellite communications support
Gains easing of US sanctions and renewed diplomatic talks
Pushes peace efforts but faces criticism over satellite restrictions
Works with Ukraine on peace ideas but is sidelined by US pressure

points: Trump says Ukraine's leader must want a deal to end the war.
Ukraine's internet satellite access was slowed, and the US is blamed.
Trump waived new sanctions on Russia, and Rubio defended the decision.
impactPoints: Ukraine faces pressure to accept a deal it may not want.
Russia gains diplomatic openings and possible easing of US pressure.
European allies are working with Ukraine to push their own peace ideas.
Other countries may feel the effects of US sanctions on Russia.

headline: Egypt involvement in Yemen 'may actually weaken Egypt's regional role', expert says
body:
What happened: Egypt's parliament delayed a vote on President Sisi's request to send military support to Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks in Yemen. An expert says the operation lacks clear goals and an exit plan, which could weaken Egypt's regional standing.

Reported by: France 24

actors.why: Military mission lacks clear goals, risking regional standing and costs.
Gains Egyptian military support against Houthi attacks on its territory.
Faces more fighting from a larger military coalition against Houthis.

points: Egypt's president asked parliament to allow military help for Saudi Arabia.
Lawmakers did not decide on the request in an emergency session.
The parliament vote was pushed back to next week.
impactPoints: Egypt could lose influence in the region if the mission goes badly.
Saudi Arabia would gain military backing against Houthi attacks in Yemen.
The Houthis face a stronger regional military response from Egypt and Saudi Arabia.
Civilians in Yemen could face more fighting and danger.

headline: Iran says no response from Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis on its mediation initiative
body:
What happened: Iran's foreign minister said Tehran has not yet received replies from Saudi Arabia or the Houthis to its mediation offer. The offer came as Iran-aligned Houthis intensified strikes on Saudi Arabia, so a diplomatic path to calm the conflict remains open but unanswered.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Al-Monitor.

actors.why: Under Houthi strikes, with no answer to Iran's mediation offer
Houthis keep striking Saudi Arabia and have not replied to talks
Its mediation offer is unanswered, but it positions itself as a peacemaker

points: Iran offered to help mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have been getting stronger recently.
Iran says neither side has answered its offer yet.
impactPoints: Saudi Arabia faces continued missile and drone attacks while talks stay unanswered.
Yemen's Houthis gain leverage if fighting continues without a deal.
Iran could look like a useful peacemaker if talks move forward.

headline: US has resumed sharing intelligence with Ukraine about Russian strikes, says Zelenskyy
body:
What happened: The US has restarted sharing intelligence with Ukraine about incoming Russian missile strikes, Zelenskyy said after talks in Oslo. The move follows a sharp US-Ukraine rift, with Trump blaming Zelenskyy for the stalled peace effort.

Reported by: The Guardian. Also covered by Al Jazeera, NPR, Japan Times, The Hindu.

actors.why: Gets warnings back but still faces missile attacks and missing Patriots.
Restored intelligence sharing but faces criticism over its policy shifts.
Keeps attacking Ukraine, though warning sharing makes strikes less surprising.
Questions US honesty as broker and backs Ukraine against US drift.
Hosted the Oslo talks, gaining a diplomatic role in the crisis.

points: US restarted sending Ukraine warnings about incoming Russian missile attacks.
Ukraine's president says the warnings help protect civilians and save lives.
The US and Ukraine have had a major falling out over peace efforts.
impactPoints: Ukrainian civilians gain earlier warning of missile strikes, which may save lives.
Russia faces less surprise but is still able to keep attacking Ukraine.
European allies worry the US is leaning toward Moscow in peace talks.
Patriot missile supply and satellite internet limits still leave Ukraine vulnerable.

headline: UK police re-arrest two men on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence
body:
What happened: UK police re-arrested two men suspected of helping Iran's intelligence service over a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, a US-used airbase in England. Police say Iranian state involvement is highly likely, though no one has been charged.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Al-Monitor.

actors.why: Base plot exposed Iranian spying; UK faces security threats and pressure.
Accused of directing plot; faces diplomatic isolation and suspicion.
Had to withdraw bombers from a UK base after the plot.
Named by UK intelligence as expanding attacks on UK military bases.

points: Police found petrol in vans near a US-used air base.
Two men were arrested again under national security law.
UK leaders blame Iran's Revolutionary Guard for the plot.
impactPoints: The UK faces pressure over Iranian spy threats on its soil.
The US pulled its bombers out of RAF Fairford after the incident.
Iran denies involvement but says attacks on bases are legitimate.
Russia is also named as expanding attacks on UK military bases.

headline: NATO to send additional patrol planes to Black Sea after drone attacks
body:
What happened: Russian drone and missile attacks have hit several cargo ships in the Black Sea, killing sailors. NATO is sending more surveillance and anti-drone assets to the region as the conflict spills toward its eastern border.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by The Guardian.

actors.why: Accused of attacks on ships; faces growing NATO surveillance in the region.
Grain shipments from its ports are being attacked, hurting its economy.
Drones entered its airspace and it is now shooting them down.
Ships were hit near its waters and it requested NATO combat aircraft.
Black Sea shipping risks and insurance costs affect its coastal waters.
Sent a maritime reconnaissance aircraft to Romania in support.

points: Russia attacked several merchant ships carrying grain near Ukraine's ports.
Some ships sank and at least 23 sailors are dead or missing.
NATO is sending planes, radar and drones to watch the Black Sea.
impactPoints: Romania shot down Russian-made drones flying over its territory this weekend.
Bulgaria asked NATO for fighter jets and anti-drone systems to protect it.
Ukraine's grain exports are at risk, which hurts its economy and food supplies.
Shipping insurance prices have jumped, raising costs for trade in the region.

headline: Republicans push back on Donald Trump’s wavering support for Ukraine
body:
What happened: Some Republicans are criticising Donald Trump for softening his stance on Russia. He waived sanctions on Moscow and agreed to buy Russian diesel, while Ukraine says it faces restricted satellite access and intelligence gaps.

Reported by: The Guardian

actors.why: Loses US support and faces restricted satellite and intelligence access.
Gains sanctions relief and a diesel import deal with the US.
Divided Congress and lawmakers threaten to block the president's agenda.
May need to shoulder more financial and military support for Ukraine.

points: Trump paused sanctions on Russia that were meant to pressure Moscow.
He also agreed a deal to import Russian diesel fuel.
Some Republican lawmakers say this is wrong and threaten to block his plans.
impactPoints: Ukraine may feel weaker and less supported by its main partner, the US.
Russia gains relief from sanctions and a new fuel trade deal.
Europe may have to carry more of Ukraine's financial and military support.
US lawmakers could push back, limiting Trump's power in Congress.

headline: As Macron visits Gulf, can France forge its own energy-for-security future?
body:
What happened: French President Emmanuel Macron is touring Gulf states to secure fuel supplies and deepen defence ties, as the Iran war disrupts global oil shipments. Kuwait, the UAE, and Bahrain have agreed to send diesel to France, and France is seeking more defence sales.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by France 24, Al-Monitor.

actors.why: Secures fuel and boosts arms exports, but faces domestic unrest.
Commits diesel supplies and deepens major defence and trade ties with France.
Signs eight agreements with France covering defence and investment.
Agrees to supply diesel to France, gaining diplomatic and economic ties.
Gets French troops to protect Red Sea oil port against Houthi attacks.
Next stop on Macron's tour, expected to strengthen energy ties.

points: Macron is visiting Gulf countries to find new fuel suppliers for France.
The Iran war has disrupted oil shipments, leaving some French petrol stations empty.
France is also trying to sell more weapons to Gulf countries.
impactPoints: France gets more diesel, easing shortages and public anger at home.
Gulf states like the UAE and Bahrain gain closer ties and defence deals.
Europe and the Gulf rely heavily on America, which may be losing influence.
Saudi Arabia gets French troops and defence help against Houthi attacks.

headline: Things Russia has done to Ukraine that Trump thinks are 'fine'
body:
What happened: Russia launched deadly drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities, killing civilians including a 1-year-old girl. US President Trump called Russia's conduct 'fine' as US support for Ukraine's air defenses reportedly weakened.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by Al Jazeera, France 24, NPR, Japan Times.

actors.why: Civilians killed and energy system targeted by Russian strikes.
Conducting mass strikes on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure.
Accused of delaying interceptors and limiting Starshield support for Ukraine.

points: Russian drones killed six people in a Kharkiv park, including a toddler.
Russia has sharply increased attacks on Ukrainian cities and civilians this autumn.
Trump said Russia has been 'fine' on Ukraine, amid rising US-Ukraine tensions.
impactPoints: Ukrainian civilians face more deadly attacks as air defenses reportedly weaken.
Ukraine's energy system is at risk ahead of winter.
US-Ukraine relations are strained over intelligence and weapons deliveries.
Russia gains room if Western support for Ukraine is reduced.

headline: JERUSALEM DAILY: Half a million Palestinians lose food aid
body:
What happened: Israeli strikes continue to kill Palestinians in Gaza while funding shortages threaten food aid for about half a million people. Reports also say Netanyahu may sideline Smotrich as settler attacks in the occupied West Bank escalate.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by The Guardian.

actors.why: Half a million people risk losing food aid amid strikes.
Strikes and settler violence bring criticism and internal political strain.

points: Israeli strikes are still killing people in Gaza.
Money for food aid is running short in Gaza.
About half a million people may lose their food help.
impactPoints: Palestinians in Gaza face hunger if food aid stops.
Israel faces pressure over strikes and settler violence.
Aid donors may be asked to fill the funding gap.

headline: Why the war on Iran could backfire on US regime-change goals
body:
What happened: Analyst Negar Mortazavi told Al Jazeera that the war on Iran could strengthen Iranian nationalism instead of sparking regime change. She argues outside attacks may unite Iranians around their homeland despite deep domestic grievances. This matters because it challenges the assumption that military pressure will weaken Tehran's government.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Asharq Al-Awsat, The National, Al-Monitor.

actors.why: Attacks could unite Iranians behind the government, strengthening its position.
Regime-change goal could backfire, making its strategy less effective.

points: An analyst spoke at the Global Security Forum.
She says outside attacks may make Iranians rally together.
Her view is that this could block regime change.
impactPoints: US plans to topple Iran's government could fail.
Iran's leaders may gain support from ordinary citizens.
Neighbouring countries could face more instability from the conflict.

headline: Lavrov backs Tehran, but does Russia also gain from the US-Iran crisis?
body:
What happened: Russia's foreign minister Sergey Lavrov pledged support for Iran in Tehran during the US-Iran crisis. Russia has also gained from higher oil prices caused by the war and from eased US sanctions on Russian energy.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Asharq Al-Awsat, Al-Monitor, Daily Sabah.

actors.why: Gains oil revenue and deepens its alliance with Iran
Gains a strong partner but faces war and closed shipping routes
Faces high fuel costs and eased sanctions on Russian energy
Took part in the attack on Iran, facing ongoing regional conflict
Gulf state pressing for shipping through Hormuz to be restored

points: Russia's foreign minister visited Tehran and promised support for Iran.
A US-Israeli war on Iran began in February and pushed oil prices up.
The US has eased some sanctions on Russian oil and diesel.
impactPoints: Russia earns much more money from oil sales during the crisis.
Iran gains a stronger partner as it fights the United States.
Gulf states want Russia to press Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
US drivers and voters may face costs, pushing Washington toward sanctions relief.

headline: Yemeni Forces Intensify Strikes against Houthis
body:
What happened: Yemeni government forces, backed by local resistance fighters, intensified strikes against Houthi positions in Taiz, Marib, and Al-Jawf. President Al-Alimi asked the UN to designate the Houthis as a terrorist group and cut their funding and weapons. Saudi Arabia and the US were also involved in the talks.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Dawn.

actors.why: Fighting, shelling, and blockades hurt civilians while government pushes back
Border attacks continue, but Saudi support to Yemen's government is praised
Gains a stronger partner role against Houthi attacks in Yemen

points: Fighting flared again around Taiz between government forces and Houthi fighters.
Government drones and airstrikes hit Houthi vehicles and positions in several areas.
Yemen's leader asked the United Nations to label the Houthis a terrorist group.
impactPoints: Yemeni civilians face more shelling, shortages of water, food, and medicine.
Saudi Arabia faces continued Houthi attacks across its border with Yemen.
The US could gain a larger role backing Yemen's government against the Houthis.
Houthi backers could face sanctions if the UN Security Council acts.

headline: Will Xi, Trump, Putin meet at Apec? First, they must agree on an agenda
body:
What happened: US President Donald Trump says he is open to meeting Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin at the Apec summit. The three-way meeting is not certain, and agreeing on an agenda is a key hurdle. A meeting would signal that Russia is ending its isolation, while worrying US allies.

Reported by: SCMP. Also covered by Politico Europe, Japan Times, Daily Sabah.

actors.why: Meeting would signal end of isolation and great-power status
Trump shows he can deal with rival powers
Hosting Apec and a possible meeting boosts Xi's leverage

points: Trump says he is open to meeting Xi and Putin.
The three leaders may not actually meet at the summit.
Agreeing on what to discuss is a key step first.
impactPoints: Russia could gain status if the three leaders meet.
A meeting would show Russia is no longer fully isolated.
Trump would look able to deal with major powers.
US allies could feel uneasy and left in unclear positions.

headline: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 200 people, sources say
body:
What happened: Drone strikes attributed to Sudan's army killed over 150 people at a fuel market in Abyei and at a funeral in West Kordofan. The disputed Abyei border area, shared with South Sudan, raises fears the conflict could spill across the border.

Reported by: BBC News. Also covered by Al Jazeera, The Guardian, France 24 Africa.

actors.why: Army accused of deadly drone strikes, facing international criticism and pressure.
Citizens hit at border market; disputed Abyei tensions escalating with Sudan.

points: Army drones reportedly hit a market in Abyei, killing 153 people.
Mourners travelling to a funeral in West Kordofan were also hit by drones.
Sudan's army has not responded to claims it carried out the strikes.
impactPoints: South Sudan is angry and has summoned Sudan's ambassador to protest.
Civilians in Sudan face deadly drone attacks and rising hunger.
UN peacekeepers in Abyei are now more exposed to danger.
Neighbouring countries fear the war could spread across borders.

headline: Rubio insists the US isn’t trying to hurt Ukraine
body:
What happened: The US Secretary of State says Washington has not changed its support for Ukraine. Ukraine's president says the US is delaying air-defense missiles and early warnings of Russian attacks. The EU's top diplomat accused US negotiators of pushing Ukraine toward surrender, raising European worries about US reliability.

Reported by: Politico Europe. Also covered by BBC News, Al Jazeera, Kyiv Independent, The Hindu.

actors.why: Faces deadly Russian attacks and shortages of air-defense missiles
Accused of delays, but denies deliberately harming Ukraine; stretched stockpiles
Escalating missile attacks while US pressure on Kyiv may favor Moscow
Worried about US reliability and forced to fill gaps in Ukraine's support
Also seeking interceptor missiles from a limited US supply
Also seeking interceptor missiles from a limited US supply

points: The US says it is not deliberately holding back help from Ukraine.
Ukraine says US missile deliveries and early warnings are being delayed.
Russia keeps attacking Ukrainian cities, and civilian deaths rose sharply last month.
impactPoints: Ukraine faces weaker air defenses against Russian missiles and drones.
European allies worry the US may not be a dependable partner for Ukraine.
Russia may gain if US pressure pushes Ukraine toward a peace deal.
The US is competing with allies like Saudi Arabia and Israel for interceptors.

headline: Zelensky prepares for Oslo talks with US envoys as Rubio denies withholding intelligence
body:
What happened: US envoy Steve Witkoff and Ukraine's President Zelensky met in Oslo amid strained ties with Washington. Zelensky complained of missing US missile warnings, which the US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected. The talks matter because they test whether the US and Ukraine can repair relations while the war with Russia continues.

Reported by: BBC News. Also covered by Al Jazeera, France 24, Politico Europe, Asharq Al-Awsat.

actors.why: Losing lives over missing warnings; relations with Washington are strained
Accused of withholding intelligence; leverage in talks but reputational strain
Gains from US mediation and strain between Kyiv and Washington
Hosting talks it hopes will steer the war toward a lasting peace
Co-hosting Oslo talks and supporting diplomacy with Ukraine
Worried about mixed US messages and carrying most of Ukraine's defence costs

points: Ukraine's President Zelensky met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.
Ukraine says the US did not always share warnings about Russian missile attacks.
US Secretary Marco Rubio denied that the US was holding back intelligence on purpose.
impactPoints: Ukraine may face more deaths if missile warnings and interceptors arrive late.
Russia hopes US talks bring a deal, but says it will not give up ground.
European countries pay more for Ukraine's defence while US support has slowed.
Oslo and Finland are helping host talks to steer relations toward peace.

headline: UK to deploy Typhoon jets to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
body:
What happened: The UK will send Typhoon fighter jets to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi missile and drone attacks, in a defensive role only. The move comes as Houthi strikes hit Saudi oil sites and Riyadh's airport, and it reflects wider concern over Gulf energy prices.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by The Guardian, Politico Europe, Le Monde, The National.

actors.why: Gets UK jets to defend cities and oil sites from attacks
Deepens military role in Gulf, but acts to protect an ally
Houthi missile and drone attacks now face a stronger defensive response
Parliament still weighing Sisi's request to support Saudi Arabia militarily

points: The UK will send fighter jets to Saudi Arabia.
The jets will only defend, not attack the Houthis.
Houthis have been firing missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.
impactPoints: Saudi Arabia gets stronger protection against missiles and drones.
Houthi rebels face a more active international defence effort against their strikes.
Rising energy prices threaten households in the UK and elsewhere.
Egypt's parliament is still deciding whether to send military support to Saudi Arabia.

headline: Turkiye moves to ratify Mecca defence pact with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
body:
What happened: Turkiye has sent a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to its parliament for ratification. The pact would require mutual help if any member is attacked, amid Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Al-Monitor, Middle East Eye.

actors.why: Gains a defence partner while facing Houthi missile and drone attacks.
Advances a strategic defence partnership, though deployment needs more approval.
Gains a closer defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
Houthi forces face a stronger regional military alliance against them.

points: Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defence agreement in August.
The pact says members must help each other if one is attacked.
Turkiye's parliament must approve it before it takes effect.
impactPoints: Saudi Arabia gains stronger backing against Houthi missile and drone attacks.
Pakistan and Turkiye gain closer military ties with Saudi Arabia.
Houthi forces in Yemen face a bigger, more united regional opposition.
Turkish troops would not deploy without separate legislation.

headline: Yemen’s Taiz faces deadly siege, as Shabwah death toll rises
body:
What happened: Houthi forces have encircled the Yemeni city of Taiz, cutting off its only supply route and threatening food for hundreds of thousands. Fighting in Shabwa killed 73 people, and Houthi missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia have prompted the UK to send fighter jets to help protect it.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by BBC News, The Guardian, Middle East Eye, The National.

actors.why: Besieged city, mounting civilian deaths and severe food shortages
Under Houthi missile and drone attacks, gaining foreign air support
Deploying jets to defend Saudi Arabia, though only defensively
Parliament delayed vote on supporting Saudi Arabia against Houthis

points: Houthi fighters have surrounded the city of Taiz in Yemen.
The only road bringing food and supplies into Taiz has been blocked.
An attack on a military base in Shabwa killed 73 people.
impactPoints: Civilians in Taiz face shortages of food and basic goods.
Saudi Arabia faces rocket and drone attacks from the Houthis.
The UK is sending fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia.
Egypt's parliament has delayed a vote on backing Saudi Arabia.

headline: US leaving oil-for-security approach, not Middle East: Envoy Tom Barrack
body:
What happened: US envoy Tom Barrack said Washington is stepping back from its old oil-for-security approach and no longer wants to control the Middle East, while not leaving. Talks between the US and Iran continue via mediators like Qatar, as the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen conflict remain flashpoints.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Al-Monitor, Middle East Eye.

actors.why: Stepping back from control, but stays involved and seeks a deal
Under war pressure and blockade, but keeps leverage and talks open
Mediating talks, gaining diplomatic role as negotiations continue
Backed by Qatar, but fighting Houthi attacks on its territory
Houthis face offensive and Saudi air strikes after seizing coastal areas
Part of the US-Israeli war on Iran, facing regional instability

points: The US wants less control over Middle East countries now.
Barrack says past attempts to change governments were mistakes.
US and Iran are still trying to reach a deal through mediators.
impactPoints: Gulf states like Qatar and Saudi Arabia must rely less on America.
Iran faces pressure from the war, but still has some leverage.
Global energy supplies are at risk while the Strait of Hormuz stays unsafe.
Yemen's Houthis are fighting Saudi-backed forces and attacking Saudi targets.

headline: Sudan drone strike kills around 150 in Abyei market
body:
What happened: A drone strike on Amiet Market in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 153 people and hit a nearby fuel depot, which kept burning. South Sudan blamed Sudan's military and summoned Sudan's ambassador, while Sudan's army did not respond. The attack raises tensions between the two countries over Abyei.

Reported by: DW. Also covered by France 24, Asharq Al-Awsat, Daily Sabah, The Hindu.

actors.why: Civilians killed and protests lodged over attack on its area
Blamed for deadly strike and summoned over civilian deaths

points: A drone hit a busy market in Abyei.
At least 153 people were killed, and many more hurt.
A nearby fuel depot caught fire and kept burning.
impactPoints: South Sudan is angry and has called Sudan's ambassador in to protest.
Sudan faces blame for the attack, though it has not commented.
Civilians in Abyei face danger and may struggle to reach hospitals.
The long unresolved dispute over Abyei could grow more dangerous.

headline: Pakistan army chief in Tehran: Can diplomacy prevent new US-Iran fighting?
body:
What happened: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir visited Tehran to push diplomacy and prevent renewed fighting between Iran and the United States. Pakistan, with Qatar's help, has mediated since the 2026 war began, but the Islamabad deal has stalled.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Al-Monitor, The National, Dawn.

actors.why: Pakistan mediates and gains diplomatic weight with both sides
Iran faces renewed war risk and blockade pressure, though it keeps talks open
US faces stalled deal and possible renewed military action against Iran
Qatar does detailed negotiating and channels proposals between US and Iran
Russia's foreign minister visited Tehran, gaining a role in talks
Israel faces possible renewed fighting with Iran and an upcoming election

points: Pakistan's army chief arrived in Tehran for talks with Iran.
He is trying to stop a new war between Iran and the US.
Earlier peace deals between the two sides have stalled and broken down.
impactPoints: Pakistan gains influence as a key mediator between Washington and Tehran.
Iran keeps diplomatic options open by talking to Russia and Pakistan.
Qatar keeps a central role in carrying proposals between the US and Iran.
Gulf states like Saudi Arabia face ongoing Houthi attacks and need protection.

headline: Saudi Arabia says it has intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh
body:
What happened: Saudi Arabia says it shot down a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh, which it blames on the Houthi militia in Yemen. The attack raises fears of wider regional fighting and tests Saudi security and its fragile truce with the Houthis.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Al-Monitor, The National, SCMP.

actors.why: Missile targeted its capital; it intercepted the attack successfully.
Houthi group blamed for firing; risks retaliation and renewed fighting.

points: Saudi Arabia says it blocked a missile heading for its capital.
Riyadh issued a warning alert just before the missile came.
Saudi officials blame the Houthi group in Yemen for firing it.
impactPoints: Saudi Arabia faces a direct threat to its capital city.
Yemen's Houthi group could face retaliation and more pressure.
Neighbouring Gulf states may worry about spreading regional conflict.
Oil markets could react if fighting in the region grows.

headline: Israeli attacks kill at least four Palestinians in Gaza
body:
What happened: Israeli air strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza, including a couple and a 17-year-old, despite a nominal ceasefire. The United Nations says most Gaza buildings are damaged, and the deaths raise doubts about the truce.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Al-Monitor, Daily Sabah, The Hindu.

actors.why: Civilians killed and homes destroyed during supposed ceasefire period
Military strikes continue, drawing international criticism and pressure
Neighbouring Egypt faces pressure from ongoing Gaza violence and aid needs

points: Israeli air strike in Gaza City killed a married couple.
A 17-year-old boy was shot dead in Khan Younis.
Another person was killed by gunfire in Zeitoun.
impactPoints: Palestinians in Gaza face continued deaths despite the ceasefire.
Ceasefire talks look weaker when attacks continue, pressuring mediators.
Israel faces criticism from neighbours and international bodies over strikes.

headline: Egypt Extends to Next Week Discussions on Military Support for Saudi Arabia
body:
What happened: Egypt's parliament delayed discussion of President Sisi's request to authorize military support for Saudi Arabia until October 26. The move comes as the Houthis launch missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia, and Britain also expands its support.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Africanews.

actors.why: Receives Egyptian and British military support against Houthi missile and drone attacks.
Must decide on sending forces abroad, with costs and risks for its security.
Expands military role with jets, transport plane and advisers in Saudi Arabia.
Houthi missile and drone strikes on Saudi Arabia escalate the conflict in Yemen.

points: Egypt's president asked parliament to approve military support for Saudi Arabia.
Egypt's parliament postponed the debate until next week for more answers.
Britain will send jets to shoot down Houthi missiles and drones over Saudi Arabia.
impactPoints: Saudi Arabia gets stronger help defending its cities and airports from Houthi attacks.
Egypt could be pulled deeper into the Yemen conflict and its costs.
Gulf and Red Sea security is tied closely to Egypt's own security, lawmakers say.
Britain is also committing more force, showing wider outside involvement in Yemen.
